name: Apologia pro Vita Sua
desc: Newman's history of his religious opinions (1865 text), written in 1864 in answer to Charles Kingsley's charge that he had taught that truth was no virtue for the Catholic clergy. Five chapters tell his life from childhood through the Oxford Movement to his reception into the Church in 1845, with the Preface, Notes A to G on liberalism, miracles, the economy and equivocation, and the additional notes and letters of the 1865 edition.
desc_pt: A história das opiniões religiosas de Newman (texto de 1865), escrita em 1864 em resposta à acusação de Charles Kingsley de que ele ensinara que a verdade não era virtude para o clero católico. Cinco capítulos narram sua vida desde a infância, passando pelo Movimento de Oxford, até a recepção na Igreja em 1845, com o Prefácio, as Notas A a G e as notas e cartas adicionais da edição de 1865.
editor: John Henry Newman (author's revised text of 1865; Newman Reader follows Longmans, new impression 1908)
edition: Apologia pro Vita Sua, being a reply to a pamphlet entitled "What, then, does Dr Newman mean?" (London: Longmans, Green, 1865 text; Newman Reader transcription of the Longmans new impression of 1908).
note: Left out: the Belloc foreword, the list of Newman's works and the empty Supplemental Matter heading. Page references in note titles ("On Page 14") are kept as Newman printed them.
